answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps each identity to a vertex in an interaction graph and requires cryptographic stake burning. Creating new nodes incurs superlinear cost scaling: registering the n-th identity forces burning a stake proportional to n^2 tokens. A validating agent shines an algorithmic lantern across transaction topologies, collapsing coordinated fake clusters into an isolated lotus structure that renders massive replication mathematically prohibitive.
